description: Haarlemmerdijk 19th-c. shop houses with WIDE multi-light windows under a white cornice: two axes, each a wide window of a centre light between narrow side lights under a top light, over a tall shop ground; 3.2-7 m fronts, eaves 8.8-10.6 m (Haarlemmerdijk 131, 133A)

match.note: Haarlemmerdijk 117-143 (2022-12-15 strip, 1 m grid): 131 rows 4.8-6.3 / 6.6-8.4 m under a cornice 9.3-9.9 m; 133A rows 5.0-6.6 / 6.9-8.2 m under a neck gable from 9.2 m. Each axis is one wide window of three lights under a top light, which measureFacade reads as 2-4 columns (5-7 over the front): columnsPerBay [2, 4]. Two axes whatever the width. crownMatch/crownStrict off as the rest of the library: reviewer crown pins decide

crowned.note: a white cornice with a small ornamented crown piece over the middle (Haarlemmerdijk 131, 173479: cornice 9.3-9.9 m, crown to 11.5 m)

door-left.note: residential ground: house door on the left axis; shops come per pand from BAG/OSM (autoShopfront)

roof.evidence: Haarlemmerdijk 131 (2022-12-15 strip): sky directly over the cornice and its crown piece; 3DBAG p95 9.91 m over a 9.6 m cornice, a near-flat roof. A front-hipped red saddle drew a roof face the strip never shows (the strip-sheet review of Haarlemmerdijk 6 rejected the same)

rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: a shop | upper: 2 wide three-light windows under top lights
rhythm.groundFloor: a tall shop ground 4.4-4.9 m to the fascia top on the dijk and straat
rhythm.roofline: a plain white cornice, sometimes one dormer
schemaLimits: the cornice frieze and consoles are a plain slab
the side lights are drawn as glazing bars of one opening, not separate frames
